doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Day two: mother, reading, LSU writing
title: The weekly short stories at LSU
summary: Audre and Amy describe his Southern short stories about LaFarge and cousin Mariana.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Audre, you were saying that Mose was writing short stories at the time, that every week he had a short story due, and every Sunday night he’d sit down and just write it out in longhand?
Yes.
Is this apocryphal, or did this happen?
That’s absolutely the truth.
I had a course at LSU, and I had to write a short story a week.
Did that filter into your songwriting, once you starting writing songs later?
I don’t know.
Writing is like a muscle. The more you write, the more it spawns further writing.
Yeah. I wasn’t writing songs at that time. I don’t know...
It might have warmed you up to it or something.
Well, yeah, it might have, because the stories were really good. They were very southern.
Do you remember what any of them were about?
I remember one of them was about Mariana, but it was describing her in New York, in her apartment. They had wonderful phrases in them. I know I didn’t throw them away; they are somewhere around.
I’ve always wanted to read them, but I don’t know where they are.

Also one... I could tell, like, characters that they were based on. One was about Taylor LaFarge, the bass player, and about what his personality was like. Do you remember that? You had the short story...
Yeah. I remember that I wrote about Taylor...
And Mariana and her cats in that apartment that you stayed in. She had all those cats.
96th and Park. She was a cat person.
[LAUGHS] Yes.
In fact, now she’s still alive with 100-and-something cats in Pennsylvania. There are lots of Southern woman characters that were in his family.
